title: per-request-reuse-signature-profiling-digest
body:
Purpose

Quick field notes on a profiling experiment to surface per-request reuse signatures (a.k.a. request fingerprints) and quantify how much eviction/pinning decisions could benefit from signature-aware policies. This is exploratory — goal is to see whether workload sub-structure is stable enough to exploit for fine-grained residency decisions without massive telemetry costs.

Background and motivation

We know aggregate reuse curves (per-model, per-seqlen) but those hide request-level patterns. Two obvious hypotheses:
- H1: A small number of request "shapes" (signature clusters) account for a large fraction of reuse and predictable KV key access patterns. If true, pin/priority policies targeted at signatures could dramatically reduce pageback.
- H2: Signatures are transient — high churn per-user/tenant — making signature-based pinning unstable and potentially harmful (pin thrash).

Approach overview

1) Trace collection: sampled full request KV access sequences (key ids) captured under production-like load on a dedicated test pool. Sampling: 1/500 requests, for 48 hours. Capture context (model, seqlen, route, time, tenant id hash).
2) Signature extraction: convert key sequence into a compact fingerprint: rolling Bloom-ish sketch + ordered first-k tokens (k=16) hashed using xxhash64 -> 128-bit signature string. Also compute a bag-of-keys frequency vector for clustering baseline.
3) Clustering: mini-batch k-means on frequency vectors (k=40) + HDBSCAN on fingerprint distances to detect natural clusters.
4) Metrics per-signature: total requests, median reuse rate (unique keys touched per 1k token-window), mean inter-arrival of identical keys, signature persistence half-life (time for signature account share to drop by 50%), bandwidth impact if pinned (estimate using per-key bytes * reuse delta).

Environment & synthetic inputs

- Hardware: p4d-like instance (8xA100 approximated), NVMe paging enabled in test harness.
- Model: mix of open-architectural Llama-variant and a conversational checkpoint we frequently use in benchmarks.
- Workloads: 3 mixes
  * Mix A: assistant-style multi-turn chat (heavy context reuse)
  * Mix B: search summarization (many short distinct prompts)
  * Mix C: mixed PLG traffic with bursty hot-keys
- Duration: 48 hr trace per mix, separate runs for single-tenant and mixed-tenant modes.

Key observations (summary)

- Cluster concentration: ~12 clusters (of 40) explain 71% of total requests for Mix A; Mix B is much flatter (top 15 clusters only 42%). Mixed traffic sits between A and B.
- Reuse skew by signature: top-10 signatures in Mix A have median per-request reuse of 3.2x vs global median 1.1x. Top signatures are dominated by long multi-turn assistant sessions where same context keys are reaccessed.
- Signature persistence: for Mix A top signatures, half-life ~14h (i.e., same signature accounts for half of its future occurrences within 14h). For Mix B, median half-life <30m.
- Bandwidth model: optimistic pinning of top-10 signatures in Mix A would reduce NVMe read-back by ~28% while increasing hot memory occupancy by ~7% (estimated). For Mix B pinning gains are negligible and can increase eviction churn.
- Unexpected: a small-but-noisy signature group in mixed-tenant runs shows high apparent reuse but is actually due to tenant-localized hotspots (single tenant generating many near-identical requests). That group disappears when we aggregate across tenants.

Representative numbers

- Sample counts: Mix A = 28,432 sampled requests; Mix B = 31,120; Mix C = 26,847.
- Unique signatures detected (HDBSCAN): Mix A = 154, Mix B = 912, Mix C = 403.
- Top-1 signature share: Mix A 18.6% of sampled requests, Mix B 4.1%, Mix C 9.7%.
- Avg keys/request (sampled): Mix A 1,360; Mix B 220; Mix C 580.

Interpretation and actionables

- Signature-aware pinning seems promising for conversational/assistant-like workloads with clear stubborn context reuse. For those tenants/routes we can consider a conservative feature: ephemeral per-signature pinning with TTL proportional to measured persistence half-life.
- For short-lived workloads (Mix B) signature churn is too high; signature policies would likely cause pin thrash and increased memory churn. For these, stick to global heuristics (LRU-ish with decay).
- Tenant isolation: before enabling signature pinning at platform level, we need tenant-aware controls — pin candidates should be filtered by tenant to avoid one noisy tenant from hogging memory.
- Telemetry budget: full sequence capture is too heavy for prod. Consider: 1) sketch-only signatures (small rolling Bloom) + periodic dense sampling; 2) edge-side lightweight fingerprints emitted by runtime (first-16 key hash) to central telemetry.

Design sketch for a runtime prototype

- On-request: compute cheap 64-bit request-fingerprint by hashing first-12 key ids + model-id + seqlen bucket. Emit to local telemetry buffer (no network call per req).
- Local aggregator: maintain per-fingerprint counters and a small LRU of pinned key sets (store canonical set for fingerprints that exceed threshold).
- Eviction policy: base LRU + signature pin overlay: when fingerprint F is pinned, keys in F get extra pin weight for TTL(F). When pins expire, keys decay.
- Safety: bound number of concurrent pinned fingerprints per device (configurable), protect high-priority tenants, and fall back to global eviction under memory pressure.

Open questions / caveats

- How to choose k for canonical key set per fingerprint? First-12 seems OK in tests but might miss tail keys that matter for reuse.
- Can adversarial tenants craft requests to get keys pinned (DoS)? Need quota and tenant isolation.
- Where to store canonical key sets for fingerprints — local memory vs. distributed metadata (latency/tradeoffs)?
- How often do pins cause cross-tenant interference in multi-tenant pools at scale? We only did limited mixed-tenant runs.
- Accuracy vs overhead trade: rolling sketches reduce payload but reduce clusterability. Need A/B tests on the production route.

Notes to self / next experiments

- Run long-tail 7-day trace with 1/1000 sampling to establish multi-day persistence stats.
- Test prototype with per-device pinned-fingerprint cap = {4,8,16} and measure steady-state NVMe read reductions vs tail latency impact.
- Implement lightweight on-device fingerprint emission (C++ low-overhead) and measure CPU overhead at 95th percentile load.
- Validate tenant-isolation heuristics: rerun mixed-tenant runs and instrument per-tenant pin impact on other tenants.

Appendix: quick method details

- Fingerprint construction: take first-k seen key ids (k=12), compute xxhash64 per id, xor combine then append a 16-bit seqlen bucket id to make a 80-bit label (we truncated to printable hex for human).
  - Frequency vector: top-200 keys per request frequency counted, normalized, then PCA -> 50d -> mini-batch k-means k=40.
  - Clustering notes: HDBSCAN on fingerprint hamming-like distance (between sketches) surfaces small dense islands we missed with k-means.

End.
